# QUESTIONs with `tags` `learning-theory`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Learning theory** — why learning generalizes and how it proceeds — compression and description length, Kolmogorov complexity and sufficient statistics, rate–distortion and PAC-style bounds, model selection; and training dynamics: solvable models of learning trajectories, stages, plateaus and phase transitions in training, and the implicit bias of optimisation. A work whose subject is how to train a model better is ML practice and goes to the anthology (ADR-036).

| [QUESTION-080](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-080.md) | When a trained network's parameters keep moving after its loss has converged, what about the network stays fixed, and is the last-layer geometry of neural collapse among the things that do? | The record holds two pictures of the end of training. In one, the last layer converges to a fixed geometry through the terminal phase ([THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), neural collapse). In the other, the parameters never stop: they sample a stationary distribution at constant speed ([THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)). The two may describe different regimes. The terminal phase of neural collapse is cross-entropy training past zero error, with no finite minimum, while the limiting dynamics assume a quadratic minimum. Nothing in the record relates them. Drawn by the assistant from the reading of Kunin et al., and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) | When the relative scale of a network's layers sets its learning regime under gradient flow, does that regime survive SGD, whose minibatch noise drives the relative scale toward balance, and on what timescale compared with learning? | Two readings meet here. Under gradient flow, the relative scale of adjacent layers is conserved and sets whether learning is rich or lazy ([THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md), Dominé et al.). Under SGD, that scale is not conserved: minibatch noise drives it toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances, at a rate set by η/S ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md), Ziyin et al.). If the drift is fast compared with learning, an unbalanced start chosen to be lazy would drift toward balance and richness. If it is slow, the regime set at initialization stands. Neither paper addresses the other. Drawn by the assistant from reading both, and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) v5 | Beyond distances and sparse recovery, whose thresholds share a sufficiency proof and not a necessity proof, when the record meets a random linear map that keeps what a later stage needs, in random features for kernels, the superposition toy model's bound and phase changes, and the expand-and-threshold codes of sparse distributed memory and the fly, is it one concentration-of-measure fact applied to different families, and does each threshold count the same thing? | Filed when a survey of the record found random projections in three places and the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma in none. The three uses carry three thresholds: ε⁻² log n for distances, k log(n/k) for sparse recovery, and 2N = n for random-features regression. The question is whether these are one union bound over different families or different phenomena that share a tool. Six anchor works are now read. They show the distance and sparse-recovery thresholds share a sufficiency proof, but not a necessity proof, and that part is [QUESTION-251](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-251.md), Answered. They give nothing that reaches random features or expand-and-threshold. For SDM and the fly, the record's SDM recall account and its LSH account offer candidate thresholds of a different shape. | Open |

| [QUESTION-133](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-133.md) v3 | Can a population of operators whose demands are jointly infeasible under one functional organization develop a differentiated or compositional repertoire that makes them jointly feasible, without suppressing, weakening or deleting any of those demands? | From the synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18, which called it the most conceptually interesting new connection. The question is whether learning, specialization or recomposition can bring this about endogenously. The record already holds that "coarse to fine" names different things: an order in training time by singular value ([THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)), an order in noise ([THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md)), and a sample-complexity result in which every level arrives at once ([THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md)). No entry separates refinement, relevance and acquisition as three relations and asks when they agree. An answer is a theorem giving sufficient conditions for a common chain, or a minimal family of counterexamples. | Open |
| [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md) v3 | Given that information-bottleneck optima at two budgets need not be nested, what condition on P(X, Y), beyond Y a function of X or X and Y both binary, guarantees that the coarser optimum is a (possibly noisy) function of the finer, X → Z₂ → Z₁, and how much is lost by forcing nesting when it fails? | A2 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which called it "the most consequential missing bridge". A hierarchy of optimal abstractions needs more than an optimum at each budget: it needs the optima to be compatible. [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) gets nesting by restricting the encoder to prunings of a fixed tree; nothing in the record says when it holds without that restriction. Rate–distortion theory's answer is successive refinability (Equitz and Cover, registered unread). | Open |
| [QUESTION-233](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-233.md) | Do language models show the data-limited exponent γ/(2β) because data limits the usable horizon: does the exponent track γ/(2β) when one corpus statistic is moved and the other held, and does the match survive at horizons of thousands of tokens with γ estimated outside the model class? | Filed when the promotion audit (batch 062, [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2 and v3) narrowed and promoted [THEORY-204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-204.md). That the fitted data-limited exponent matches γ/(2β) on TinyStories and WikiText-103, and that assumed per-lag scaling forms give min(δ, γ/(2β)), is settled. Whether real learners show the exponent for the horizon reason was the old promote_when, and it moves here. | Open |
| [QUESTION-236](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-236.md) | Does fixed-feature transfer to new classes fall as penultimate class separation rises outside ImageNet-trained ResNet-50s, and does it move with within-class spread when the loss is held fixed? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md), moved unchanged when that account was narrowed to what Kornblith et al. (2021) measured and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). Open: whether the inverse relation between penultimate class separation and new-class transfer holds in other pretraining settings, and whether separation, rather than the loss, is what moves transfer. | Open |
| [QUESTION-244](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-244.md) | Must the optimal representations of an information-bottleneck objective at two budgets be nested, so that the coarser optimum is a (possibly noisy) function of the finer? | The yes-or-no part of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). No, for deterministic encoders ([CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md)) and for stochastic ones ([CLAIM-392](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-392.md)), on one four-state source with binary Y. Raising the budget can reorganize the optimum rather than split it. What condition on P(X, Y) guarantees nesting stays with [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-251](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-251.md) | Do the Johnson–Lindenstrauss threshold for distances and the k log(N/k) threshold for sparse recovery rest on one concentration-of-measure argument, a tail bound for each fixed vector's norm with a union bound over a family, both for sufficiency and for necessity? | The part of [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) its readings on distances and sparse recovery settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For sufficiency, yes: one per-vector tail and a union bound give both, over pairs for distances ([THEORY-397](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-397.md)) and over net points on every sparse support for recovery ([THEORY-390](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-390.md)). For necessity, no: the distance lower bounds are encoding and bit-counting arguments ([THEORY-395](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-395.md), [THEORY-399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md)), recovery's rests on Gelfand widths, and its sharp location on face counting ([THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md)). Random features, superposition and expand-and-threshold stay with [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-271](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-271.md) v5 | How can an organization evaluate its own processes so that the evaluation decides authority without being captured by it: when wins among the processes cycle, when no common scale scores them all, when the processes in charge can add, filter or duplicate the tests, and when only the processes heeded are evaluated? | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-24, with the registration of works from multi-agent reinforcement learning and learning in games, after the owner asked how the record stands on MARL. The governance line keeps returning to one gap: the scoring that allocates authority is itself governed. The replicator construction makes that gap a lock-in threshold, and BoostTheVote assumes it away with an objective metric. The question asks what evaluation procedures resist capture, and in which of four senses. | Open |
| [QUESTION-275](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-275.md) v2 | Can the development of a transformer's circuits in training be described as organizational regimes forming over shared, overlapping latent features, so that a model coupling feature allocation to circuit interaction, fitted to early checkpoints, predicts the effects of held-out training interventions that feature-only and circuit-only descriptions fitted to the same checkpoints miss? | The owner, at T24: "could we potentially apply this setup as an interpretive framework for understanding the learning dynamics of transformers?" "This setup" is the dynamic latent-feature model of T23 ([CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md)). The reply answered with a test: "Can the emergence, specialization, overlap, and persistence of transformer circuits be explained by modeling them as developing organizational regimes over shared latent features—and does that description predict training responses that existing feature- or circuit-based analyses miss?" It is the second time the owner has applied the record's frameworks to a network in training. The first was [CASE-113](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-113.md) and [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md), and [CASE-117](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-117.md) is the population form. The sharp edge is [CLAIM-427](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md)'s third grade: positive results would have to be prospective, against strong conventional baselines at matched complexity. Nothing here says that a circuit is a perspective. | Open |
| [QUESTION-291](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-291.md) | For finite X and Y, does every finite-budget information-bottleneck optimum nest under the β → ∞ optimum, what test on a pair of optimal encoders decides whether two finite budgets nest, and do the optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X or when X and Y are both binary? | The settled part of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md), [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) and [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) (Active) answer it. Every finite-β optimum is a stochastic coarsening of the causal partition. Two budgets nest iff some pair of optimal encoders forms X → T₂ → T₁, a convex-hull test on decoder points. The optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X and when X and Y are both binary. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-305](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-305.md) | From small random weights not aligned with the data's eigenbasis, does a linear-attention layer trained on in-context regression come into alignment with that basis before or while its modes are learned, so that its learning is staged by the input spectrum without the alignment being assumed? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md), moved here when the ninth status review narrowed it to the aligned case it derives and promoted it, as [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md)'s moved to [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md). [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) holds the same open claim for two-layer linear networks. | Open |
| [QUESTION-312](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-312.md) | Does linear mode connectivity emerge during training rather than at initialization outside image classification and beyond MLPs: in a language model or transformer, for copies spawned from a shared state and for independent runs aligned under the architecture's symmetry group, and for standard-width convnets or ResNets after alignment? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md), moved here when the tenth status review narrowed it to the image-classification networks and MLPs its two sources measured and promoted it, as [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md)'s moved to [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md). | Open |
| [QUESTION-338](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-338.md) | Measured on another game, or on Hex with a standard AlphaZero implementation or larger networks, is the iso-strength trade between training compute and tree-search compute again a straight line in log–log space ending at a one-node search, and is its slope, reported with its uncertainty and with test-time compute in a stated unit, within error of Jones's −1.2? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md), moved here when the status review of 2026-10-30 promoted it under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md). Jones measured one game with one nonstandard implementation and gave no uncertainty on the slope, and he asks twice for the test on other games. | Open |
| [QUESTION-349](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-349.md) | On tasks other than Jacobs and colleagues' four-class vowel discrimination, do mixtures of experts trained on the error of a single expert chosen stochastically by the gate, or on the mixture's negative log-likelihood, leave most experts with near-zero mixing proportions while matching the accuracy of a dense network of equal size? | The replication [THEORY-937](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md)'s promotion condition asked for, moved here when the twenty-third status review promoted that reading of one study ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3: a request to replicate moves to a QUESTION). The vowel task needs two or three lines; whether the sparse division appears on tasks without so few natural subtasks is open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-361](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-361.md) v2 | Is an organization's recursive production usefully understood as self-distillation, each realization generating a specification of its own effective organization that constrains how its successor is built, and if so, what makes the distillation the organization's own rather than run by an outside optimizer, and what makes a successor a good teacher as well as a faithful student? | The owner's proposal at U15 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "maybe framing this recursive production as self-distillation could be helpful or at least interesting?", with Teoh's multi-token-prediction paper ([LIT-1896](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1896.md)). A15 and A16 developed it as "organizational inheritance". It refines [QUESTION-016](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-016.md), which asks when iterated reconstruction preserves task-relative sufficiency, by adding who runs the reconstruction and whether the successor can carry it on. | Open |
| [QUESTION-363](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-363.md) | When does the order in which stochastic gradient descent comes to occupy a network's organizations over training time follow the order in which they come to dominate the Bayesian posterior as the sample grows, and what fixes the correspondence where it holds: an effective temperature set by learning rate and batch size, the accessibility of regions and the barriers between them, or the time allowed to equilibrate? | The owner's challenge at U4 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). A3 had said that "Bayesian posterior dominance as sample size n changes is not the same process as gradient-based optimization as training time advances". The owner: "Isn't it? I think there's a David M Blei paper that discusses this." The paper is Mandt, Hoffman and Blei 2017 ([LIT-1898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md)). A4 conceded the separation was "too strong" and kept a narrower one, which is this question. It refines [QUESTION-039](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-039.md), which asks what sets the order and moment of acquisition. | Open |
| [QUESTION-492](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-492.md) | In networks trained on relational-rule tasks under varied data diversity, does the emergence of role abstraction (a quotient of inputs by token relabelling) coincide with balanced-partition (fibration) structure among the network's units, or can either occur without the other? | The owner's, from U9 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" (2026-11-18): "I have a hunch this fibration approach relates nicely to" Li and Webb's study of what drives symbolic mechanisms ([LIT-2830](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2830.md)). The fibration approach is the balanced-partition theory of synchrony the record holds as [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) and [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md), which the owner had just met in Gili et al. ([LIT-2804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2804.md)). A21 sharpened the hunch: both are quotients that keep the operations that matter, one of inputs by relabelling, one of units by equal input trees. Li and Webb, read, say nothing at the level of units or partitions, so the link is untested. The question's wording is the filer's; the hunch is the owner's. | Open |
| [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md) | In a percept–action loop with feedback, does the memory that minimizes dissipation retain the interventional partition of histories (the causal information bottleneck), the predictive partition, or neither, once the costs of building, maintaining, operating and revising it are counted? | A's, from A65 §4 and §9–10 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" (2026-11-19), after the owner asked to "connect this to information thermodynamics" (U29) and remarked "sounds like we're getting into active learning territory now" (U30). Still and colleagues relate dissipation to nonpredictive memory only for a system driven without feedback ([THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md)). The causal information bottleneck's optimum is the partition by response to intervention ([THEORY-1125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1125.md), [THEORY-1146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1146.md)), which A65 rebuilt as an "intervention-response signature". A proposed an "intervention-relative, physically costed information bottleneck" and called it a proposal, not a theorem. A learner that chooses its observations breaks the no-feedback condition, so the passive result does not reach it. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-495](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-495.md) | What would make a learning process optimal, when some of the most valuable consequences of learning are changes in what the learner can later learn, ask and afford, which cannot be specified in advance; and when is investing in future learnability better than improving present competence? | The owner's, from U21 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" (2026-11-19): "how might we formulate a notion of 'optimal learning'", after U20: "I feel like we're reasonably appropriately situated to make general claims about how learning works". A48 answered with a context-relative definition and an open problem; A50 §8 and A71 §13 asked the narrower form, when learning widens the frontier of future learning rather than concentrating present competence. The record holds the parts: capability trajectories ([CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)), the conditional value of keeping a corrective capacity ([CLAIM-520](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md)), resource-indexed repertoires ([CLAIM-576](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-576.md), [CLAIM-697](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-697.md)), and the questions a realized specification makes askable ([CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md)). The question's wording is the filer's, joining the owner's U21 to A's open problems. | Open |
| [QUESTION-497](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-497.md) | When what a learner retains is identifiable but not localized, or localized but not identifiable, which of the two, if either, fixes the boundary of the learner and its individuation by its learning history? | The owner's question (2026-11-19), from the discussion of in-context learning under [TERM-131](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-131.md) version 2. It first contrasted learning merely persisted into a stable representation with learning that is concretely indexable, then sharpened that to identifiability against localization. [CLAIM-765](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-765.md) holds that the two come apart. This asks which of them the boundary and identity of a learner follow. | Open |
| [QUESTION-502](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-502.md) | Do networks trained with orthogonalized updates, steepest descent in the spectral norm, learn the structure of their data in a different order from networks trained by gradient descent: is the coarse-to-fine progressive differentiation that gradient descent shows on hierarchically structured data weaker, absent or reversed? | [CLAIM-774](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-774.md) shows that in a two-layer linear network, equalizing the rates of singular directions within a layer reverses and compresses the order in which modes are learned. Saxe and colleagues read the gradient descent order as progressive differentiation of a hierarchy of categories ([THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)). Whether the reversal survives nonlinearity, depth, momentum and noise, and shows in networks trained with such updates in practice, is open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-504](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-504.md) | Does help that maximizes the user's long-horizon influence, as a stabilizing shared-autonomy assistant does, erode the user's unassisted capacity, and can command-to-outcome information taken with the assistance present ever show it? | Raised by [CLAIM-787](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-787.md). [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) holds that where capacity is learned by doing and decays with disuse, support that does the work can erode it; a score taken with the support present cannot see that. | Open |
| [QUESTION-507](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-507.md) v3 | Do systems near a dynamical transition, or with scale-free dynamics, have a distinctive computational capacity, or does nearness to the transition only redistribute a bounded capacity among kinds of computation, by task? | A's open direction at the close of A13 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", "whether scale-free systems have a distinctive computational capacity—whether their multiscale correlations make them especially capable of storing memories, propagating signals, adapting, or performing calculations", which A calls "considerably more subtle" than the edge of chaos, and which A15 takes up. The record holds the order-to-chaos transition in deep networks ([THEORY-2041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2041.md), [THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md)), a reservoir ([THEORY-1431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1431.md)) and 1/f in brains ([CLAIM-692](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-692.md)), and no question on criticality and computation. The wording is A's (the other assistant in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", A13 and A15); adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-510](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-510.md) | What replaces singular learning theory's fixed-dimension asymptotics, n → ∞ with the parameter count held fixed, when width or parameter count grows in proportion to the data, and does a learning coefficient estimated in that regime still measure the singular geometry? | A37 §9 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" (2026-11-21): "classical RLCT asymptotics cannot be directly transplanted into a regime where network width or parameter count grows proportionally with the amount of data", so a combined theory "may need to track at least three scales", γ = D/N, an effective dimension and a local learning coefficient. A flags the mismatch and gives no theory for it; every combined test A proposes depends on it. The wording is A's (the other assistant in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", A37); adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-511](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-511.md) | Does recent work on the informativeness of small-eigenvalue subspaces during learning bear on the signature of a transition the exchange proposed, in which a previously weak direction becomes informative, a local degeneracy changes and a new distinction becomes independently decodable? | The owner's U25 in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" (2026-11-21). It quotes A39's proposed signature of a transition ("a previously weak direction becomes informative, a local degeneracy changes, and a new semantic distinction becomes independently decodable") and adds: "I think there's been some recent work in the informativeness of small-eigenvalue subspaces during learning that might be relevant here". The question is the owner's pointer, put as the question it raises. The ordering of the three events and the sorting of "weak" by spectrum are A41's, set out in the body as A's. | Open |
| [QUESTION-512](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-512.md) | Can entailment cones help reason about progressive learning dynamics, the order in which a network comes to draw finer distinctions? | The owner's, at U21 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" (2026-11-21): "i wonder if considering entailment cones might help us reason about progressive learning dynamics". A sharpening of [QUESTION-217](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-217.md)'s coarse-to-fine question by a geometric tool, the nested cones of hyperbolic entailment embeddings, which the record holds as a construction ([THEORY-189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-189.md)) but not as a lens on training. | Open |
| [QUESTION-514](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-514.md) | Does the incidence order of a network's singular strata, which stratum lies in the closure of which, map onto the order in which its representations refine one another, and how far from one-to-one is the map? | A37 §6, A39 §§7–8 and A43 §14 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" (2026-11-21): the hypothesis that "the stages of hierarchical representation learning correspond to transitions among functionally distinct strata of a singular neural-network model", sharpened into a map Φ from strata to a semantic partial order. A says it "requires a model-specific construction". The assistant adds the smallest construction where the strata and their incidence can be stated. The wording is A's (the other assistant in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", A37, A39, A43); adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-515](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-515.md) | What follows if the representational manifold a deep network learns, a high-dimensional system, is modelled as an active-matter system? | The owner's, at U18 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" (2026-11-21): "how about if high dimensional systems? consider a representational manifold learned by a DNN modeled as an active matter system". The other assistant's answer (A29 §11) grades the idea into three hypotheses of increasing strength, which the body sets out as A's, and the owner's next turn (U19) adds concentration of measure as the baseline any such model has to beat ([CLAIM-822](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-822.md)). | Open |
| [QUESTION-517](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-517.md) | Do the effective dimensions of one system, the number of its stiff Fisher directions at a given resolution, the dimension of its predictive states, the number of its relevant renormalization-group directions and its fractal dimension, agree, and when do they come apart? | A's open question at the close of A19 and the table at A21 §1 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws": "Is the effective dimensionality of a complex system fundamentally determined by how much information is required to predict its behavior?", with "several competing meanings of effective dimensionality: geometric dimension, the number of important Fisher-information eigenvectors, the number of predictive state variables, and the number of relevant RG directions. Understanding when these quantities agree—and when they diverge" is the task. The record holds pieces of each and no comparison; [QUESTION-217](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-217.md) asks a sibling question about orders, not counts. The wording is A's (the other assistant in the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", A19 and A21); adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-518](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-518.md) | What do decreases of the local learning coefficient during training correspond to, in the model's structure and in the singular-learning account of stages? | Raised by the reading of Hoogland and colleagues ([NOTE-2248](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2248.md), [THEORY-2160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2160.md)): three of their ten stages are decreases of the estimated local learning coefficient, which their motivating account does not produce and which they call an open problem. Neither reading of the owner's U23 ([CLAIM-834](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-834.md)) accounts for them. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
